:::{#def-matrix-power}
#### Matrix power

For a square matrix $\matr{A}$ of order $p$
and a positive integer $k$,
the $k$-th **power** of $\matr{A}$ is:

$$\matr{A}^k = \underbrace{\matr{A}\,\matr{A}\cdots\matr{A}}_{k \text{ copies}}$$

In particular, $\matr{A}^2 = \matr{A}\matr{A}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-matrix-power}
#### Powers of a $2 \times 2$ matrix

Let $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$. Then

$$
\ba
\matr{A}^2
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 0 & 1 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 1 \\ 0 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 0 & 0 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 1 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(definition of matrix multiplication)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix},
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\\
\matr{A}^3 = \matr{A}^2 \matr{A}
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \cd 1 + 2 \cd 0 & 1 \cd 1 + 2 \cd 1 \\ 0 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 0 & 0 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 1 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(definition of matrix multiplication)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}.
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

A $2 \times 3$ matrix $\matr{B}$ is not square (@def-square-matrix), so $\matr{B}^2$ is not defined;
indeed $\matr{B} \matr{B}$ would multiply a matrix with $3$ columns by one with $2$ rows,
which @def-matrix-mult does not allow.

:::
